step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture starts with smart fire hydrants (acting as ThirdParty IoT devices) capturing daily acoustic signal data from water pipe networks. These devices push daily data files through Amazon API Gateway for security and ingestion authentication. Once authenticated, the files are written and persisted into Amazon S3. On a daily batch cycle, Amazon ECS runs containerized microservices to process the files using processor-intensive acoustic correlation algorithms. Identified persistent correlations are then sent to an Amazon SageMaker machine learning endpoint to calculate leak probability scores. Human analysts (User) review these scores to coordinate leak qualification with local utilities.

edges.notes: Daily acoustic files are uploaded securely via API Gateway.
Persists and stores daily uploaded acoustic data files in Amazon S3.
ECS pulls and processes the raw acoustic data daily as node pairs to check for correlations.
ECS forwards persistent correlations to SageMaker ML endpoint for classification.
SageMaker leak score and classification is surfaced to human analysts for review.
